title: Efficiency from a polynomial-time test
statement: Let $M$ be a Boolean-valued function of two finite Boolean strings, and let $t$ be a Boolean-valued function on finite Boolean strings. Suppose the function that maps each string $z$ to the one-symbol output containing $t(z)$ is computable in polynomial time, and suppose $t(\langle x,r\rangle)=M(x,r)$ for every pair of strings, where $\langle x,r\rangle$ is formed by doubling each bit of $x$, appending the separator $01$, and then appending $r$. Then the verifier that accepts exactly when $M(x,r)$ is true is efficient in the polynomial-time verifier model.
hypotheses_covered: $M$ maps pairs of finite Boolean strings to Boolean values
$t$ maps finite Boolean strings to Boolean values
the one-symbol-output function $z\mapsto[t(z)]$ is polynomial-time computable
$t(\langle x,r\rangle)=M(x,r)$ for every pair of finite Boolean strings
